m_more_ahead.text: More of them up ahead. Twelve o'clock — here they come.

m_low_on_water.text: Fighters low on the water, six o'clock. They followed us out.

m_one_more_time.text: Pilot to crew, one more time. Fighters, twelve o'clock high, a lot of them!

rc_next_wave.text: Here comes the next wave, look sharp!

p4_tutorial_7.text: You're ready, gunner! Welcome to the crew of the Sky Queen.

p4_tutorial_8.text: This is a training flight, gunner. Nobody shoots back today. See that target drone? Put your sight on it.

p4_tutorial_9.text: Short bursts! Watch your tracers and walk them in.

p4_tutorial_10.text: Lead him! Aim where he's going to be, not where he is.

p4_tutorial_11.text: Use the ring sight for the long ones. Hold the right button.

p4_tutorial_12.text: Fighter on the other side! Somebody get on that gun!

p4_tutorial_13.text: Navigator here. Watch the radar plot — and Tab gives you the big picture.

p4_tutorial_14.text: Nice shooting. The ground crew fitted you something extra.

p4_tutorial_15.text: Here they come — three bandits. Show me what you've learned!

p4_bossbattle_16.text: That's the last of them! Scratch one battle group — drinks are on me!

p4_bossbattle_17.text: You got it just in time!

p4_bossbattle_18.text: Nice shooting — that broke it up!

p4_bossbattle_20.text: Jesus, that was close! She nearly took our tail off!

p4_bossbattle_21.text: Turret knocked out! Keep at it!

p4_bossbattle_22.text: Rocket pod went up like a firework!

p4_bossbattle_24.text: Fighters dropping out of that thing's belly!

p4_bossbattle_25.text: She's breaking up! That's the last of them!

p4_bossbattle_26.text: Look at her go — she's breaking in two!

dressing.text: Hold still — I've patched you up. Back on that gun.

mode_ace.text: That one's an ace — kill markings all down the tail. Watch him!

sp_zdone.text: That's the last of the destroyers! Nice work, boys.

sp_barrage.text: Rocket barrage! Heavies standing off at a kilometre — they'll keep lobbing rockets into the box until we knock them down!

sp_bdone.text: Launchers are down! That's the end of the rockets.

sp_bout.text: They're out of rockets — the heavies are heading home.

sp_acewings.text: The yellow noses are breaking off — they've lost their leader!

pace_lot.text: That's the lot of them! They're breaking off!

pilot_1.text: He's reversing — scissors! Throttle back, make him fly out in front!

pilot_2.text: Head-on! Hold your fire till he's close, then break high!

pilot_3.text: Watch it, Blue two — his wingman is sliding in behind you!

pilot_4.text: He's spiralling down — don't follow him into the deck!

pilot_5.text: Focke-Wulf's zooming up for another pass. Keep your speed!

pilot_6.text: Thanks, little friend — he was all over us!

pilot_7.text: We owe you one, little friend. We're going to make it!

pilot_8.text: Bandits twelve o'clock low, climbing for the bombers. Get between them and the big friends!

pilot_9.text: Little friends, twin-engine bandits closing at our six — they've got rockets!

pilot_10.text: Another gaggle, nine o'clock level. Some of them are coming for us!

pilot_11.text: Heads up — 109s high at six, coming down on us! Break and engage!

pilot_12.text: Bandits on the bombers, twelve o'clock! Little friends, where are you?

pilot_13.text: Focke-Wulfs diving out of the sun — don't try to out-climb them!

pilot_14.text: Bandits going for the cripple! Blue two, get back there and cover her!

pilot_15.text: More of them coming in on our tail — we can't take another pass!

pilot_16.text: One last pass at the box, twelve o'clock. Let's finish this!

pilot_17.text: Big gaggle at twelve o'clock — drop tanks and go! Hit them before they reach the box!

pilot_18.text: Zerstörers at six o'clock, with rockets! Get them off us!

pilot_19.text: Jets! Twelve o'clock high, fast movers — go for them when they slow down!

pilot_20.text: Messerschmitts, high at five o'clock! Here they come — break!

pilot_21.text: Jets coming through! You won't out-run them — turn inside them!

pilot_22.text: Fighters on the bombers, twelve o'clock level!

pilot_23.text: They're sending another Gruppe down on us. Stay together!

pilot_24.text: They're on the straggler! Blue two, cover her, I'll take the box!

pilot_25.text: Jet coming up our tail! Somebody get him off us!

pilot_26.text: Last push — they're throwing everything at the box!

bk_clear.text: Deenethorpe tower to Sky Queen: you are cleared for take-off. Good hunting.

bk_flying.text: Ninety… one-ten… she's flying! Gear up.

bk_climb.text: Pilot to crew: climbing through the overcast. We form up on top.

bk_letdown.text: Pilot to crew: letting down through the overcast. We're nearly home.

bk_land.text: Sky Queen, you are number one to land. Welcome home.

bk_crash_crew.text: Crash crew, stand by! Ambulances to the runway!

bk_belly.text: The gear won't come down — brace for a belly landing!

bk_home.text: Home in one piece. Nice work, everybody.

raid_flares.text: Control: pathfinder flares going down over the field! The bombers will aim on them — get under the flares and you'll see them.

wx_front_g.text: Storm front dead ahead. Tighten it up — we're going right through it.

wx_front_p.text: Blue flight, storm front dead ahead. Close it up and stay on my wing in the murk.

wx_clear_g.text: We're breaking out of the cloud — clear sky ahead. They'll see us coming now.

wx_clear_p.text: Blue flight, the cloud's breaking up. Clear sky ahead — keep your eyes open.

bk5_spotted__nav.text: Me 410 hanging back out of range — he's carrying a fifty-millimetre cannon!

bk5_spotted__bigfriend.text: Me 410 hanging back out of range — he's carrying a fifty-millimetre cannon!

raid_he111_nav.text: German bombers crossing ahead — a whole formation of Heinkels!

strafe_r1.text: Control to Blue flight: a supply train is heading east for the tunnel. Stop that locomotive before it gets there!

strafe_r2.text: Control: a truck convoy is on the road to the village. Shoot it up before it gets under cover!

strafe_r3.text: Control: the Luftwaffe field to the north-east. Strafe the aircraft on the ground — and watch the flak!

strafe_loco.text: Got the loco! She's blown her boiler!

strafe_escaped.text: The train made it into the tunnel. Too late, Blue flight.

strafe_flak.text: Light flak coming up! Stay low and keep jinking!

strafe_bandits.text: Focke-Wulfs coming down on us! Watch your tail, Leader!

strafe_wing_go.text: Blue Two, going down on your target!

strafe_wing_kill.text: Blue Two — got one on the ground!

strafe_area.text: Blue Leader, you are leaving the target area. Come back round.

sp_flak_hit.text: Direct hit on the ship next to us! Her wing's folding up!

sp_flak_spin.text: She's rolling over… she's going into a flat spin. Get out, fellas — get out of there!

sp_chutes_few.text: That's all. Ten men on that ship… God help the rest of them.

sp_chutes_many.text: That's all I see. Come on… come on… that's all of them.

sp_ram_warn.text: That one-ninety's on fire — he's not pulling out! He's going to ram her!

sp_ram_hit.text: He hit her! Oh God, they're locked together!

sp_ram_down.text: They're going down together… I don't see anybody getting out.

sp_ram_chute.text: One chute! One man got out!

sp_ram_saved.text: Got him before he hit her! That was too close!

sp_bay_fire.text: She's hit in the bomb bay — she's burning! She's going to blow!

sp_bay_wing.text: Wing section coming past the window — look out!

sp_bay_gone.text: She's gone. The whole ship… just gone.

sp_bay_check.text: Crew, check in! Is anybody hurt back there?

sp_strag_feather.text: She's feathered two engines — she can't keep up! She's dropping out!

sp_strag_plea.text: They're chewing us to pieces back here! For God's sake, somebody help us!

sp_strag_lost.text: She's going down… we couldn't do a thing for her.

sp_lf_lead.text: Big friends, hold your fire — Mustangs coming through!

sp_lf_pass.text: Little friends! Right past the window — they're all over him!

sp_lf_kill.text: They got him! God bless those little friends!

cr_dp1_1__nav.text: We kept the sun on the right and flew south. Africa still feels like another world.

cr_dp1_1__copilot.text: We kept the sun on the right and flew south. Africa still feels like another world.

cr_dp1_3__top.text: The engines need work before we cross the sea again. Tonight, at least, they can cool down.

cr_dp1_3__waist.text: The engines need work before we cross the sea again. Tonight, at least, they can cool down.

cr_dp2_1__ball.text: I saw the bomb bay open in a sheet of fire. I cannot get that window out of my head.

cr_dp2_3__radio.text: I left the radio on until the last landing. I kept hoping to hear another call sign.

cr_dp2_2__pilot.text: Sit here a while. Nobody has to tell the story twice tonight.

cr_dp3_1__tail.text: Those Mustangs stayed. I asked the cook to keep two extra plates.

cr_dp3_1__copilot.text: Those Mustangs stayed. I asked the cook to keep two extra plates.

cr_dp3_3__nav.text: An escort is more than a mark on the briefing map. Today we saw the men behind it.

cr_dp3_2__top.text: Then let them eat first. We can wait for once.

cr_dp4_3__radio.text: I will put the chart beside the stove. Let it dry before we fold it away.

cr_dp4_2__waist.text: Leave the hole. We know the way back now.

cr_dp5_1__bombardier.text: All those tanks below us, and I only remember the ship beside us.

cr_dp5_1__copilot.text: All those tanks below us, and I only remember the ship beside us.

cr_dp5_3__tail.text: The new boys asked whether it gets easier. I told them we learn to look after each other.

cr_dp5_3__waist.text: The new boys asked whether it gets easier. I told them we learn to look after each other.

cr_dp5_2__pilot.text: Write down the names before the numbers. That is how we finish this book.

cr_dp5_2__nav.text: Write down the names before the numbers. That is how we finish this book.

cr_m1_1.text: Well, that's one. First thing tomorrow I'm painting a bomb under the window.

cr_m1_2.text: I counted forty-one holes in her. Forty-one, and not one of them in us.

cr_m1_3.text: Emden on the first try. I said I would.

cr_m1_4.text: Told you. Nobody can find me down in that ball.

cr_m1_6.text: My hands didn't stop shaking till we crossed the English coast. Is that normal?

cr_m1_7__pilot.text: It's normal. Mine haven't stopped yet.

cr_m1_7__copilot.text: It's normal. Mine haven't stopped yet.

cr_m1_8__pilot.text: Get some sleep, all of you. One down. Twenty-four to go.

cr_m1_8__copilot.text: Get some sleep, all of you. One down. Twenty-four to go.

cr_m2_1.text: They came straight at the nose. All I could see was the propeller hub and the guns winking at me.

cr_m2_2.text: That top turret earned its keep today. Twin fifties, and somebody who knew what to do with them.

cr_m2_3.text: Lieutenant, you've been humming the same four bars since we landed.

cr_m2_4.text: It helps. Don't ask me why. It helps.

cr_m2_5.text: Two down. I'm keeping the tally in the back of my navigation log.

cr_m2_6.text: Fog's coming in. Maybe they'll stand us down tomorrow.

cr_m8_1.text: They came for the Lucky Lady's things an hour ago. Folded the blankets. Took the photographs off the wall.

cr_m8_2.text: Their tail gunner owed me two dollars. I'd give anything for him to walk in here and not pay it.

cr_m8_3.text: Sixty Fortresses. Six hundred men. I keep doing the arithmetic, and it keeps coming out the same.

cr_m8_4.text: From the ball I could see the chutes. I tried to count them. I couldn't keep up.

cr_m8_5.text: I lit a candle for them in the chapel. I didn't know what else to do.

cr_m8_6.text: Still got the rabbit's foot. I don't know if that makes me lucky, or them not.

cr_m8_7__pilot.text: We came home. Tomorrow we'll think about why. Tonight, try to sleep.

cr_m8_7__copilot.text: We came home. Tomorrow we'll think about why. Tonight, try to sleep.

cr_m9_1.text: There he is. The Mustang that stayed with us all the way to Kiel. Sit down, sir. Dinner's on me.

cr_m9_2.text: For a month, Hawkeye. You said a month. The whole ship heard you on the interphone.

cr_m9_3.text: I know what I said. Worth every penny.

cr_m9_4__pilot.text: We couldn't see our own wingtips in that front. When the Germans came through the gaps, you were already there.

cr_m9_4__copilot.text: We couldn't see our own wingtips in that front. When the Germans came through the gaps, you were already there.

cr_m9_5.text: The first time anyone's gone all the way with us. It changes the arithmetic.

cr_m9_7.text: To the little friends. May they never run short of fuel.

cr_m9_8.text: Same time tomorrow, sir? I'll bring my wallet.

cr_m3_1.text: Two hundred guns down there, and I still put the bombs right on the aiming point. I've never seen flak like it.

cr_m3_2.text: Merry Christmas, Ray. Five days late.

cr_m3_3.text: Every gun had its Saint Christopher today, and every one of us came home. I'm not saying it's the medals. I'm not saying it isn't.

cr_m3_4.text: On Christmas Eve I kept thinking about the Lucky Lady's boys. They'd have liked the snow.

cr_m3_5.text: Tomorrow is the last day of the year. Nineteen forty-four, gentlemen.

cr_m3_6.text: Next Christmas at home. Everybody say it.

cr_m10_1.text: I kissed that runway, and I'd do it again. The RAF boys think I've gone flak happy.

cr_m10_2__pilot.text: They took Frank to the hospital. The surgeon says he'll keep the leg.

cr_m10_2__nav.text: They took Frank to the hospital. The surgeon says he'll keep the leg.

cr_m10_3.text: I told you. I wasn't putting an old lady in the Channel on her thirteenth.

cr_m10_4.text: When the Spitfires showed up off the coast, I could have cried. Maybe I did.

cr_m10_5.text: Somebody write to Frank tonight. Tell him the old lady made it.

cr_m10_6.text: I'll write it. I'll make it long. He hates long letters.

cr_m10_7__pilot.text: Lights out. We fly home in the morning.

cr_m10_7__nav.text: Lights out. We fly home in the morning.

cr_m4_1.text: Leipzig and back, and not one of them got through to us. I said there was a steak in it, didn't I?

cr_m4_2.text: He's been saving his coupons for a week. Don't ask him where he found a steak in England.

cr_m4_3.text: Big Week, they're calling it. The whole Eighth went out today, all of us after the aircraft factories.

cr_m4_4__pilot.text: When that Fortress fell out of formation, I thought she was finished. Then you came down on the wolves.

cr_m4_4__nav.text: When that Fortress fell out of formation, I thought she was finished. Then you came down on the wolves.

cr_m4_5.text: Frank wrote from the hospital. He says the nurses are lovely and the food is a crime.

cr_m4_6.text: There's a rumour we're going back to Schweinfurt. Nobody say it out loud.

cr_m4_7.text: Eat your steak, sir. You earned it.

cr_m5_1.text: Schweinfurt. There, I said it. Somebody had to.

cr_m5_2.text: A hundred yards. I could see the rounds sparking off their windscreens, and they still didn't break.

cr_m5_3.text: I've got my piece of Frankfurt on my key ring. It came up through the floor and found my leg. I'm keeping it.

cr_m5_4.text: Sixty ships stayed behind the last time. Today we brought ours home. That's enough for me.

cr_m5_5.text: Nineteen missions. Six to go. I don't like saying the number out loud either.

cr_m5_6.text: Same socks tomorrow. Don't anybody say a word.

cr_m5_7__pilot.text: Long day tomorrow. Lights out in ten minutes.

cr_m5_7__copilot.text: Long day tomorrow. Lights out in ten minutes.

cr_m11_1.text: Right on the aiming point. I've seen the photographs. The assembly hall is gone.

cr_m11_2.text: He's shown everybody the photographs. Twice. He showed the barman.

cr_m11_3.text: I waited nineteen missions for that target. I'm entitled.

cr_m11_4.text: Four minutes straight and level through that flak. I said it in September and I'll say it now. I do not like flak.

cr_m11_6__pilot.text: Every Messerschmitt they don't build is one that won't be waiting for the next crew. Remember that.

cr_m11_6__copilot.text: Every Messerschmitt they don't build is one that won't be waiting for the next crew. Remember that.

cr_m11_7.text: Buy the man a drink. Even if he is insufferable.

cr_m6_1.text: Two engines, all the way across Holland. I listened to every cylinder the whole way home.

cr_m6_2__pilot.text: Twenty-two missions, and she carried us home again.

cr_m6_2__copilot.text: Twenty-two missions, and she carried us home again.

cr_m6_3.text: When the Mustangs came over the horizon, Price started laughing and couldn't stop.

cr_m6_4.text: Wasn't laughing. Something in my eye.

cr_m6_5.text: The ground crew has been out there since we landed. In the rain, with lamps. They say she'll be ready by Wednesday.

cr_m6_6.text: Somebody take those boys a thermos of coffee. They've earned it more than we have.

cr_m7_1.text: Berlin. We went to Berlin and back, and the Mustangs never left us.

cr_m7_2.text: I saw a Fortress with a crown on her nose get a lot of extra cover today. Somebody told you, didn't they?

cr_m7_3.text: I painted that crown. I'm taking the credit for the whole escort.

cr_m7_4.text: They say the Luftwaffe lost more today than it can replace. You could feel it. They didn't press like they used to.

cr_m7_5__pilot.text: The ground crew put her back together in two days. She flew today with every man who wouldn't leave her.

cr_m7_5__nav.text: The ground crew put her back together in two days. She flew today with every man who wouldn't leave her.

cr_m7_6.text: I've stopped pretending I don't count the missions. We're close now.

cr_m7_8.text: And put it on my tab.

cr_m12_1.text: I rubbed out the pencil. It's in paint now. Twenty-five bombs under the window.

cr_m12_3.text: I went out to her after we landed and put my hand on number three engine. Still warm. I said thank you.

cr_m12_4.text: I'm going to miss the ball. Don't tell anybody I said that.

cr_m12_5.text: I'm burning these socks. Out behind the hut, a proper funeral.

cr_m12_6.text: Twenty-five missions. I've worked it out a dozen ways, and it never adds up to why we came home and the others didn't.

cr_m12_7__pilot.text: I want to say something about the Lucky Lady's boys. And the new crews who never finished their first week.

cr_m12_7__copilot.text: I want to say something about the Lucky Lady's boys. And the new crews who never finished their first week.

cr_m12_8__pilot.text: We knew some of their names. Not all of them. We carry them home anyway.

cr_m12_8__copilot.text: We knew some of their names. Not all of them. We carry them home anyway.

cr_m12_9.text: Twenty-five missions and never a scratch. I think about that more than I should.

cr_m12_10.text: First thing, I'm going to stand in the middle of the cornfield and look at the sky. Just look at it.

cr_m12_11.text: The ranch will still be there. Cattle don't know there was a war.

cr_m12_12.text: Brooklyn. My mother's going to cook for three days, and I'm going to let her.

cr_m12_13.text: Boston. I'm singing at my sister's wedding, and this time I'll know all the words.

cr_m12_14.text: Philadelphia. A classroom full of kids who think arithmetic is boring. God bless every one of them.

cr_m12_15.text: San Antonio. I'm going to fix my father's truck, and nobody is going to shoot at me while I do it.

cr_m12_16.text: I'm going to sleep for a week. Then I'll think about it.

cr_m12_17.text: Kansas. Low and slow over the wheat, and nobody shooting.

cr_m12_18__pilot.text: It was an honour to fly with every one of you. Thank you.

cr_m12_18__copilot.text: It was an honour to fly with every one of you. Thank you.

cr_gun_0.text: Didn't get one today? Don't let it eat at you. Every burst you fired kept one of them off us.

cr_gun_1.text: You got one today. Some fellows fly ten missions and never see one fall.

cr_gun_3.text: The low squadron saw you knock them down, one after another. They're asking who was on that gun.

cr_gun_5__radio.text: Five or more in one day. They're putting your name in for the Cross, and I'm telling everybody I know you.

cr_gun_5__ball.text: Five or more in one day. They're putting your name in for the Cross, and I'm telling everybody I know you.

cr_acc_high.text: You shoot like a man who's paying for his own shells.

cr_acc_low__top.text: The armourers say you nearly burned out a barrel. Short bursts. Let the gun cool between them.

cr_acc_low__ball.text: The armourers say you nearly burned out a barrel. Short bursts. Let the gun cool between them.

cr_fly_0__tail.text: You didn't get one? Doesn't matter. Every time one of them saw you coming, he broke off.

cr_fly_0__ball.text: You didn't get one? Doesn't matter. Every time one of them saw you coming, he broke off.

cr_fly_1__tail.text: I watched you from the tail. You came down on them like a hawk on a chicken run.

cr_fly_1__ball.text: I watched you from the tail. You came down on them like a hawk on a chicken run.

cr_fly_5__radio.text: Five or more, the way Dawson tells it. Somebody paint a row of crosses under that canopy.

fbk_clear.text: Boxted tower to Blue flight: you are cleared for take-off. Good hunting.

fbk_rv.text: Blue flight, Big Friends at twelve o'clock low. Take station on the box.

fbk_break.text: Blue flight, initial for the break. Breaking left.

fbk_land.text: Blue flight, cleared to land. Welcome home.

fbk_wheelsup.text: Gear won't come down — I'm putting her down on her belly!

fbk_crash.text: Crash crew to the runway! Mustang coming in wheels up!

fbk_home.text: Blue Four is down. Nice flying today, Two.

bombardier_good.text: Good pattern! The aiming point is covered.

bombardier_poor.text: The pattern is wide. We will check the strike photograph.

ditch_1.text: We're not going to make it — prepare for ditching.

ditch_2.text: Crew in ditching positions. Brace! Brace!

ditch_3.text: Everybody out! Launch the dinghies and stay together.

ditch_4.text: Rescue launch in sight! Firing a flare.

ditch_5.text: All ten accounted for. Picked up by the RAF Air-Sea Rescue.

sea_start.text: Blue flight, ships ahead. Rockets for the escorts; save your bombs for the waterline.

sea_dive.text: U-boat crash-diving! Put a bomb alongside before she gets deep!

sea_boss.text: Battleship ahead! Silence her guns, then hit the magazines at the waterline.

sea_salvo.text: Main guns tracking us! Break away from the marked area!

sea_radar.text: Radar is down. Their flak crews are aiming by eye now.

aa_inbound.text: Control to gun crews: raiders inbound. Protect the tower and the parked Fortresses!

aa_major.text: Control: major raid approaching. All gun pits, open fire!

aa_repair.text: Control: raid broken up. Repair crews, move out!

gs_oxygen.text: Oxygen check! Reconnect your mask hose, gunner!

gs_jam.text: My gun's jammed! Working the charging handle!

gs_ammo.text: Need ammo at the waist! Pass another can!

p8t_sturm.text: Wedge at twelve! Armoured Focke-Wulfs, level! Open fire early!

p8t_hornisse.text: Me 410s at one kilometre! Keep firing at the heavy cannon ships!

p8t_airbomb.text: Fighters holding high at twelve! Air bombs! Top turret, stop them dropping!

p8t_jet.text: Jets slashing in from six! Tail gunner, take the brief shot!

p8t_axes.text: Three and nine together! Pick one pair and break their attack!

ss_type_fw190.text: Butcher-birds. Watch for the head-on pass.

ss_type_bf109.text: Messerschmitt one oh nines. Quick in the turn.

ss_type_bf110.text: Messerschmitt one tens. Heavy twins, rear gunners.

ss_type_ju88.text: Junkers eighty eights. Armoured twins, keep firing.

ss_type_me262.text: Two sixty two jets. Fast, but fragile.

ss_type_me163.text: Komet rocket fighters. Very fast, lightly built.

ss_type_he111.text: Heinkel bombers. Gunners in every window.

ss_type_me410.text: Hornisse twins. Watch that fifty millimetre cannon.

ss_type_do335.text: Dornier push-pull fighters. Fast in a dive.

ss_revenge_wound.text: He's back. The ace who wounded our crew. Watch him!

ss_revenge_down.text: He's back. The ace who shot us down!

ss_ace_in.text: Yellow noses, twelve o'clock high! That's the ace's Staffel!

ss_ace_out.text: The ace is breaking off. Yellow noses heading home.

ss_ace_kill.text: You got the ace! The whole group saw him go down!

ss_ace_other.text: Somebody got the ace! Scratch one Experte!

ss_rear.text: Careful, Blue two. That twin has a rear gunner. Come at him from below!

ss_cover.text: Little friends, we've lost two engines and can't keep up. Can you cover us?

ss_break_left.text: He's seen you — he's breaking left! Stay with him!

ss_break_right.text: He's seen you — he's breaking right! Stay with him!

ss_check.text: That pass is over. Crew, check in.

ss_hurt.text: We've got wounded back here. I'm helping them. Keep those fighters off us.

ss_clear.text: Tail checking in. Guns clear. Still with you.

ss_quiet.text: Just the engines and the wind. Keep watching that cloud bank.

ss_miss.text: Your burst went behind him. Give him more lead.

ss_kill.text: Good shooting. Saw that one break apart.

lf_damage.text: Number two is feathered. We are holding station.

lf_straggler.text: We are dropping back. Keep those fighters off us!

lf_lead.text: Deputy lead taking over. Close up on me.

lf_reform.text: Box is re-formed. Keep your spacing.

lf_ditch.text: We cannot make the coast. Putting her down in the sea.

lf_kill.text: Got him! He is going down behind the box.

br_ip.text: Initial point inbound. Fighters are pulling back. Hold formation.

br_steady.text: Steady. Straight and level. No evasive action.

br_doors.text: Bomb bay doors open. Cold air coming through.

br_cloud.text: Target hidden by overcast. Bombing on the lead ship.

br_markers.text: Target markers in sight. Smoke from the earlier wave.

br_count.text: Five seconds. Steady. Three. Two. One.

br_rally.text: Rally point. Close the bays. Fighters coming back!

br_hit.text: Flak hit the ship beside us! Her engine is burning!

dc_fuselage.text: Fire in the fuselage! Waist gunners, get the extinguisher!

dc_bombBay.text: Fire in the bomb bay! Get forward with the extinguisher!

dc_runaway.text: Runaway propeller! Engineer, feather that engine!

dc_controls.text: Control cables hit. Help me hold her steady!

dc_fireOut.text: Cabin fire is out. Keep those guns covered.

dc_aid.text: Coming aft with the first aid kit. I will take his gun.

dc_ammo.text: Bringing another ammunition can down the catwalk.

ai_sig_l_corkscrew.text: He's corkscrewing through his run! Wait for him to level out, then hit him!

ai_sig_k_corkscrew.text: That's his corkscrew! Hold fire till he levels out!

ai_sig_l_splits.text: He rolled over and split-S'd under the box! He goes out low!

ai_sig_k_splits.text: Here comes his split-S! Ball turret, catch him going down!

ai_sig_l_zoom.text: He pulled straight up after his pass! He hangs up there at the top!

ai_sig_k_zoom.text: He'll zoom up again! Top turret, wait for him at the top!

ai_sig_l_wingover.text: He wingovered straight back in! He comes at the same gun again!

ai_sig_k_wingover.text: Same trick — he'll wingover and come right back! Stay on him!

ai_sig_l_lowsix.text: He snuck up low at six! Watch under the tail!

ai_sig_k_lowsix.text: His low-six trick again! Tail and ball, watch under us!

ai_weak_tail.text: He's going for our tail — the tail gunner's hit! Somebody cover six!

ai_weak_waistl.text: He's lining up on the left waist — that gun's hurt! Cover nine o'clock!

ai_weak_waistr.text: He's lining up on the right waist — that gun's hurt! Cover three o'clock!

ai_weak_top.text: He's diving on the top turret — the engineer's hit! Cover the top!

ai_weak_ball.text: He's coming up under us — the ball turret's hurt! Cover the belly!

ai_limp.text: That one's hit — he's limping home, trailing smoke!

ai_press.text: He's smoking but he's coming back in — finish him!

ai_broke.text: You drove him off — he broke away!

ai_pair.text: Pair coming in, one behind the other! Stay on the gun!

tour_mail.text: Mail call! Letters from home for everybody.

tour_fog.text: Fog on the field. Nobody's flying today.

events28_nearMiss_1.text: Watch it — she's sliding right into us!

events28_nearMiss_3.text: Missed us by a wingspan. Somebody buy that pilot a drink.

events28_friendlyExplodes_1.text: Ship in the high squadron — she's hit in the fuel tanks!

events28_friendlyExplodes_3.text: Logging it. Keep your eyes outside, everybody.

events28_bailout_1.text: She's going down — count the chutes, everybody!

events28_bailout_2.text: Good. They'll sit the war out in a camp. Better than the alternative.

events28_jamming_1.text: They're jamming us — the whole band's gone to static!

events28_jamming_2.text: Interphone's weak. Call bandits by the clock — loud and clear!

events28_oxygenFire_1.text: Fire! The oxygen line's burning in the radio room!

events28_oxygenFire_2.text: Extinguisher's on it — shut that oxygen valve!

events28_oxygenFire_3.text: It's out. Lost a bottle, but it's out.

events28_gunnerFreezes_1.text: Waist gun's quiet — he's frozen up on the gun!

events28_gunnerFreezes_2.text: Snap out of it, son! Get back on that gun!

events28_gunnerFreezes_3.text: I'm okay… I'm back on it. Sorry, sir.

events28_salute_1.text: One-oh-nine sliding up on our tail — he's hit bad!

events28_salute_2.text: He's not shooting. He's right off our wing…

events28_salute_3.text: He's saluting us. Hold your fire. Let him go.

events28_lostMustang_1.text: Big friend, this is a lost little friend. Mind if I tag along?

events28_lostMustang_2.text: Come on in, little friend. Glad to have you.

events28_cookOff_1.text: Her waist ammo's cooking off — rounds going everywhere!

events28_cookOff_2.text: They're throwing the boxes out the window!

events28_cookOff_3.text: She's still flying. Tough old girl.

events28_weatherWall_1.text: Weather wall dead ahead — tops above thirty thousand. No way over it.

events28_weatherWall_2.text: Then we go through. Close it up and watch your spacing.

events28_flakWalk_1.text: Flak's tracking us — they've got our altitude!

events28_flakWalk_3.text: That threw them off. The bursts are falling behind.

events28_runawayProp_1.text: Ship off our wing — runaway prop, she's smoking bad!

events28_runawayProp_2.text: She got it feathered. She's holding formation.

events28_redFlares_1.text: Red flares from the ship off our wing — wounded aboard!

events28_redFlares_2.text: She lands first. Let's get her home.

events28_enemyBailout_1.text: Burning Fw 190 coming across — he's in trouble!

events28_enemyBailout_3.text: Let him go. His war's over.

events28_yellowNoses_1.text: Yellow noses at twelve o'clock — the Abbeville boys! Head-on!

events28_yellowNoses_2.text: Top turret, chin turret — get on them!

events28_sunBandits_1.text: Bandits in the sun! Coming down high — watch the glare!

events28_sunBandits_2.text: Squint and lead them. They have to come out of it sometime.

events28_chaff_1.text: Lead's dropping chaff — foil strips to blind their radar.

events28_chaff_2.text: Look at it glitter. Christmas over Germany.

events28_oxygenCheck_1.text: Oxygen check. Sound off, tail to nose.

events28_tightenUp_1.text: All ships, close it up! Tight box — mass your guns!

events28_tightenUp_2.text: That's better. Every gun in the box covers us now.

events28_strayTracers_1.text: Hey! Watch your fire — that's a friendly ship!

events28_strayTracers_2.text: Some kid in the next ship's got the jitters.

events28_escortHome_1.text: Big friend, I'm hit — coolant's going. Turning for home.

events28_escortHome_2.text: Good luck, little friend. Thanks for the company.

events28_brassRain_1.text: Brass coming down from the ship above — it's raining shell casings!

events28_brassRain_2.text: Keep your heads down and your guns up.

enemies24_night.text: Ju 88 Gs coming in — radar night fighter — attacks from below with upward-firing cannon!

enemies24_below.text: Night fighter below us! Watch his upward cannon!

brief_m1_1.text: Gentlemen, this is your first one. The group puts up eighteen ships against the U-boat yards at Emden. Bombing altitude twenty-five thousand feet.

brief_m1_2.text: You are left waist gunner aboard the Sky Queen, number two ship in the lead element. Expect single-engine fighters over the Frisian coast. They will come in fast and they will come in close.

brief_m1_3.text: Lead your target. A fighter crossing at three hundred miles an hour needs a lot of lead — watch your tracers and walk them in. Short bursts. Keep that barrel cool.

brief_m1_4.text: A word about your ship. The Sky Queen is brand new, and so is her crew. Captain Brenner flies her, Lieutenant Stern has promised to find Emden on the first try, and Sergeant Gallo has already painted a crown under the pilot's window. Twenty-five missions and you go home. This is number one.

brief_m2_1.text: The Luftwaffe has learned that the nose of a Fortress is its weak spot. Their fighters are making head-on passes at closing speeds of six hundred miles an hour.

brief_m2_2.text: You are flying the top turret today. Twin fifties, three hundred and sixty degrees of traverse. When they come in from twelve o'clock high you are the man who has to stop them.

brief_m2_3.text: Bremen is heavily defended. Expect repeated attacks before and after the target.

brief_m2_4.text: The Sky Queen came back from Emden with forty-one holes in her and not a scratch on her crew. Sergeant Reilly says the ball turret is the safest seat in the house, because the Germans cannot find him down there. Lieutenant Doyle says nobody else can either. Mission two. Keep it off the interphone once we cross the coast.

brief_m8_1.text: Gentlemen, the target is Schweinfurt. Half the ball bearings in Germany come out of five factories in one small town. Flatten them, and every tank, U-boat and fighter in the Reich will feel it. The Eighth is putting up nearly three hundred Fortresses, and the Luftwaffe knows we are coming.

brief_m8_2.text: The escort turns back at Aachen. After that we are on our own for two hundred miles, and intelligence expects every fighter group in western Germany to be waiting: single-engine fighters head-on, twin-engine destroyers firing rockets from astern. They will hit us in relays, land, refuel and come up again.

brief_m8_3.text: You are in the ball turret today. Keep it turning, keep calling them out, and watch the bellies of the low squadron. Nobody else can see what is coming up from below.

brief_m8_4.text: This is the Sky Queen's third mission. Lieutenant Doyle wants it on the record that he volunteered for a milk run and nobody offered him one. Fly tight. Today a tight formation is the only escort you will have.

brief_m9_1.text: Until now the bombers have gone into Germany alone the moment the escort ran short of fuel. As of today that changes. The Mustang can reach Kiel and come home again, and you are going all the way with them.

brief_m9_2.text: The weather is the worst we have flown in. A front lies across the North Sea from the Frisian Islands to Denmark: towering cloud, icing above eight thousand feet and lightning in the tops. We take off in clear air, and you will see it ahead long before we reach it. Once we are in, stay on your leader's wing in the murk. The German fighters will come at the bombers through the gaps.

brief_m9_3.text: The bomber crews are watching you today. The Sky Queen's tail gunner, Sergeant Dawson, has seen too many friends go down after the escort turned for home. He says that if a Mustang sticks with them all the way to Kiel, he will buy its pilot dinner for a month.

brief_m9_4.text: Mouse aim flies the aeroplane where you look. Keep your speed up, do not chase them into the cloud, and stay with the big friends.

brief_m3_1.text: The I.G. Farben works at Ludwigshafen is ringed by more than two hundred heavy flak guns. There is nothing you can do about flak but pray — and keep the fighters off us. The forecast has the overcast breaking up short of the target, so the gunners down there will have a clear view of us.

brief_m3_2.text: You are right waist gunner. Fighters will hit us on the way in, then pull off when we reach the flak belt. Once bombs are away, they will be back for the cripples.

brief_m3_3.text: Stay at your gun through the bomb run. Do not get out of position.

brief_m3_4.text: Since Schweinfurt the bunks across the aisle have changed names twice. The Lucky Lady never came back from that one, and her crew had been with the Sky Queen since training. Sergeant Mendez has blessed every gun aboard with a Saint Christopher medal. Lieutenant Kessler wants only one thing for Christmas: the aiming point.

brief_m10_1.text: Frankfurt is burning behind us, and so is the Sky Queen. Flak over the target knocked out two engines and put Lieutenant Doyle on the floor of the cockpit with a piece of steel in his leg. The group could not wait for us. We are alone, low on fuel, and the sun is going down.

brief_m10_2.text: Lieutenant Stern has plotted the shortest line home: across Belgium and out over the Channel past Dunkirk. Every fighter field in Flanders sits under that line. Sergeant Gallo is calling Air-Sea Rescue every five minutes, and the crew has thrown out everything that is not bolted down, except the guns.

brief_m10_3.text: The Germans love a straggler at dusk. They will come out of the dark side of the sky, low over the water where you cannot see them against the sea. Watch the east, and use every gun position, one through five.

brief_m10_4.text: Fighter Command has promised an escort off the coast. Hold out until it gets here. Captain Brenner says this is the Sky Queen's thirteenth mission, and he is not putting an old lady in the Channel on her thirteenth.

brief_m4_1.text: Big Week. The whole Eighth Air Force is going after the German aircraft industry, and this time the bombers will not go alone.

brief_m4_2.text: You are flying a P-51D Mustang on close escort for a box of twelve Fortresses. First the Focke-Wulfs and Zerstörers will go for the bombers — intercept them before they reach the box. Then expect a fighter sweep of 109s hunting the escort, flying in pairs: watch for the wingman. And if a Fortress falls out of formation, the wolves will go for her. Do not let them.

brief_m4_3.text: Mouse aim flies the aircraft toward where you look. W and S for throttle, V for cockpit or chase view, T padlocks the nearest bandit. Your six fifties are harmonised at two hundred and fifty metres — get in close.

brief_m4_4.text: Some of you met the Sky Queen's crew in the pub at Oundle after Kiel. Their tail gunner, Sergeant Dawson, is still paying for dinners for the Mustang pilots who went all the way with them. He says there is a steak in it for anyone who sees them home from Leipzig.

brief_m5_1.text: Intelligence reports a new kind of German unit: the Sturmgruppe. Heavily armoured Fw 190 A-8s that close to point-blank range from astern, in line abreast, and do not break off.

brief_m5_2.text: You are the tail gunner. They will be coming straight at you. Open fire early and keep firing — armour glass in their windscreens will stop a lot of what you throw at them.

brief_m5_3.text: The Sky Queen is one of the senior ships in the group now, with eighteen missions behind her. Lieutenant Doyle is back from hospital with a piece of Frankfurt flak on his key ring, and nobody aboard will say the word Schweinfurt out loud. The last time we went there, sixty Fortresses stayed behind. Not today.

brief_m11_1.text: This is the last day of Big Week, and the target is the one the group paid for so dearly in August: the Messerschmitt works at Regensburg. Every Bf 109 that has come at you this week was built under that roof. Today we take the roof off.

brief_m11_2.text: The plant is ringed by heavy guns, and they will fire a box barrage straight up the bomb run. From the initial point to bombs away is four minutes of straight and level flying. No evasive action. The Sky Queen holds her place in the formation and takes it.

brief_m11_3.text: Lieutenant Kessler has waited nineteen missions for a target like this. He spent the night with the target photographs and says he could find the assembly hall in his sleep. Your job is to keep the fighters off him until he does. You have the top turret, and they will come for the lead ships from above.

brief_m11_4.text: Sergeant Mendez has asked me to remind everyone that he does not like flak, and that he has been saying so since September. Noted, Sergeant. Bombs away is what this whole war is about. Make it count.

brief_m6_1.text: Flak over Berlin knocked out two of our engines. We cannot hold formation and the group is pulling away from us. A lone Fortress is exactly what the Jagdflieger are looking for.

brief_m6_2.text: Every gun aboard is manned. Switch positions as they come in — one through five. P-51s are on the way to pick us up, but we have to hold out until they get here.

brief_m6_3.text: Sergeant Gallo is calling every station that will listen. Lieutenant Stern has us on a heading for the coast, and Captain Brenner has told the crew that the Sky Queen did not carry them through twenty-one missions to let them down now. Hold on.

brief_m7_1.text: This is the big one. The Luftwaffe is throwing everything it has left at the bomber stream over Berlin.

brief_m7_2.text: You lead the escort for our box. Rocket-armed Zerstörers will try to break up the formation, then the 109s and the new jets will come for the escort. The Me 262 is faster than anything we have — do not chase it, turn inside it and catch it when it comes back round. Bf 110s carry a rear gunner: come at them from below.

brief_m7_3.text: Over the target a crippled Fortress will need you. Pick your targets, protect the bombers, and keep your speed up.

brief_m7_4.text: The Sky Queen made it home on two engines two days ago. The ground crew worked on her all night, and she is flying today with the men who would not leave her. When you see a Fortress with a crown painted under the cockpit, give her a little extra cover. She has three missions to go.

brief_m12_1.text: Gentlemen, this is a maximum effort. Big Week broke the back of the German fighter arm; today we finish the job. More than nine hundred heavy bombers are going after the aircraft plants at Oschersleben, Bernburg and Stettin, and the Luftwaffe will throw everything it has left at us.

brief_m12_2.text: There are Mustangs all the way to the target now, so the Germans hit the bomber stream before the escort can join. Expect a heavy attack on the way in, flak over the target, and a last fight before the little friends arrive. Hold on until they get there.

brief_m12_3.text: For the Sky Queen this is mission twenty-five. When she lands, her crew goes home. Lieutenant Doyle is back in the right-hand seat with a new limp and the same old jokes, and Sergeant Gallo has already painted the twenty-fifth bomb under the cockpit window. In pencil, he says, so it does not count as bad luck.

brief_m12_4.text: You are back on the left waist gun, where you started at Emden. Think of the crews who are not here today: the Lucky Lady over Schweinfurt, and the new boys who never finished their first week. Fly this one for them. Then come home, all of you.

brief_dp1_1.text: On 17 August 1943, the Eighth Air Force attacks Regensburg and Schweinfurt. Our force strikes the Messerschmitt works at Regensburg, then continues south across the Alps to North Africa. Fog has delayed the Schweinfurt force; the intended diversion is coming apart.

brief_dp1_2.text: The short-range escort cannot follow us deep into Germany. Expect Fw 190s and Bf 109s from both beams, with Bf 110s behind. Cover a damaged Fortress falling out of the box before we reach the assembly halls beside the Danube.

brief_dp1_3.text: This chapter revisits historical raids with our fictional crew and existing aircraft. Combat time and geography are compressed. After bombs away, hold the southern course: this sortie ends on the shuttle route, not back in England.

brief_dp2_1.text: On 14 October 1943, the Eighth returns to the ball-bearing factories at Schweinfurt. The August raid did not stop production for long. Once the escort turns back, the Fortresses must fight their way to the target and out again without fighter cover.

brief_dp2_2.text: Expect repeated single-engine attacks and rocket-carrying Bf 110s and Ju 88s. Watch the high fighters: they may drop bombs into the box. Switch to the top turret to interrupt them, then cover the low squadron through the bomb run.

brief_dp2_3.text: The long factory roofs and rail sidings mark the aiming area. A neighbouring ship will be hit in the bomb bay; keep clear of the wreckage and hold your station. The crew will remember the empty bunks after this one.

brief_dp3_1.text: Operation Argument opens on 20 February 1944. The Eighth strikes aircraft factories across Germany; our objective is the Leipzig aircraft industry. Assembly sheds and the nearby airfield stand out against the winter ground.

brief_dp3_2.text: Long-range escort now reaches deeper into Germany. Keep firing until the Mustangs arrive. Me 410 heavy fighters may stand off with cannon while the single-engine fighters close; the top turret must cover both threats.

brief_dp3_3.text: Two little friends will dive past the formation to clear a pursuer. Check your fire as they cross. Dawson has kept his promise to buy an escort pilot dinner; tonight he may finally get to pay the bill.

brief_dp4_1.text: On 6 March 1944, a major American bomber force reaches Berlin. The earlier attempt on 4 March had been reduced by weather. Today the industrial districts and railway network lie at the end of a long, heavily defended route.

brief_dp4_2.text: Escort reliefs cover the stream, but the enemy can still converge from three and nine together. Pick one pair and break its approach. No jets are expected on this March raid; the danger is coordinated conventional fighters and heavy flak.

brief_dp4_3.text: A damaged fighter may tumble into the box. Stop it before it strikes a Fortress. Beyond the mist, follow the broad street grid and rail yards through the bomb run, then stay alert for attacks on the return leg.

brief_dp5_1.text: On 2 November 1944, the oil offensive returns to the Leuna synthetic fuel works near Merseburg. Fuel shortages are hurting German flying and training, but the refinery is still producing. Its tank farms and processing blocks are our aiming area.

brief_dp5_2.text: Merseburg is protected by concentrated heavy flak. Armoured Fw 190 formations and Bf 109s remain dangerous; late-war jets may make brief passes. Keep the tail guns ready, and switch forward when the armoured wedge assembles.

brief_dp5_3.text: A Fortress beside us will take a direct flak hit. There is no fighter to shoot at in that moment: stay steady and protect the survivors. The target is fuel production; the crew's measure of success is how many men come home.
